name: Machine Reverse Fly
summary: A seated machine isolation exercise targeting the posterior deltoids and upper back musculature through horizontal shoulder abduction.

setup: Adjust the machine handles fully back so they start in front of the chest when seated facing the pad.
Adjust the seat height so that the handles sit at mid-chest to shoulder level.
Sit facing the chest pad with your torso firmly supported, feet flat on the floor, and grasp the handles with a neutral or pronated grip and a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
steps: Brace your core and initiate the movement by pulling your arms backward and outward in a wide horizontal arc.
Continue horizontally abducting your shoulders until your upper arms are roughly in line with your torso, squeezing the rear deltoids.
Pause briefly at peak contraction without hyperextending your lower back.
Control the handles as you reverse the arc back to the starting position, maintaining tension on the rear deltoids before the weights touch down.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and backward; inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
cues: Lead with the back of your elbows.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows throughout.
Push your chest gently into the pad, not away from it.

common_faults.fault: Excessively bending and extending the elbows like a triceps press.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight bend into your elbows at setup and maintain that exact angle across the entire range.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears.
common_faults.correction: Depress your shoulders and lower the seat slightly so your hands track below shoulder level.

common_faults.fault: Arching the lower back off the chest pad to heave the weight.
common_faults.correction: Keep your sternum pressed firmly into the pad and reduce the working weight to isolate the shoulders.

precautions: Avoid letting the machine jerk your arms past your active range of motion into deep horizontal adduction.
